answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks, AI agent networks enforce a stake-backed execution protocol where nodes sign a 14-phase computational challenge, termed a sonnet, using a hardware-bound private key acting as a digital quill. As consensus data undertakes its validation voyage across peer nodes, attackers attempting identity cloning incur prohibitive costs, as each Sybil instance requires locked economic collateral and verified non-reproducible hardware proofs.
